content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is low or trending downward; adjust downward by 1–2% for consecutive low sentiment days.
- Underestimate sharp price spikes (especially >5% from prior day) when sentiment is high; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for such events.
- When sentiment drops below 0.30, reduce forecast mean by 0.5–1.5% to account for downward momentum.
- Forecast mean reversion is stronger in 10–14 day horizons; apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline.
- Overshoots after spikes (especially >70) are common; cap forecast at 10% below peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is rising (last 3 days > 0.60), forecast should be slightly higher than 30-day average; add 0.5–1.5% to mean if sentiment > 0.70.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3 days show high volatility, reduce forecast sensitivity to 1–2 day history.
